items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-07-14
items.q: Poor Santo, when we were playing with Sharky

ctx.x: Well, you couldn't spend any money on the boat, huh, Much? No. Did you gamble? Oh, no. I never gambled. I would think that'd be one thing to do on the boats, river boats. That's traditional.

When I was playing with Tony Foucherat and Mutt Powers and Flavor Ford, like I told you, we were playing in Smack Over Arkansas at one time. No. Tony wasn't in that band. I was with Happy Cook and Little Chink Martin, Charlie DuPont, Harry Shields. When we were playing at a gambling place about five miles out of Smack Over Arkansas, when gambling was strictly against the law, on New Year's Eve night, I saw a man walk out after losing everything in the world he had. I couldn't get to him in time. He blew his…

items.title: Santo Pecora Interview, 1972-11-09
items.q: So he made up a band, he got Jeff Riddick, Lester Bouchard, Jake Martin, and he had Diggalane, you know, and he had a girl singer, see.

ctx.x: Meal and Minutes. Meal and Minutes. Yeah.

I was a little bit of a band called Bill Gruber. So they only wanted a four piece band because it was a small stage, smaller than the famous door, see. So they only had four pieces. So I had to leave Sharky go and let the Bouchard go, see. So it was trombone, piano, drums and bass. So when I got finished there, Sharky, Monk Hazel, you know how Sharky got in the famous store? Monk Hazel told Hip, he said, man why don't you put a Dixieland band in this? He said, you're not making money with that Spanish band and…
How many jobs would you work a day with Sharky then?

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: Now, this is the first band at the famous door. Mm-hmm. Santo.

ctx.x: Yeah. It had nothing to do with that.
Now, this is the first band at the famous door. Mm-hmm. Santo. And Lester's got his tenor.
Yeah. He's got his clarinet there. Yeah. Yeah. I never saw Chink play tuba there. Did he ever play tuba?
